title: Polynomial-time density estimation for arbitrary Gaussian mixtures
formal: Can every mixture of k Gaussians in ℝ^d be learned to total-variation error ε from independent samples in time and sample size polynomial in d,k,1/ε, without separation, weight or covariance-conditioning promises?
definitions: The target distribution is Σ_{i=1}^k w_i N(μ_i,Σ_i), with w_i≥0, Σ_i w_i=1 and positive-definite covariance matrices. Total-variation distance between densities f and g is one half the integral of |f−g|. The learner may output a distribution outside the mixture class. The degree of the running-time polynomial must be independent of k, and parameter recovery is not required.

context_blocks.text: Gaussian mixtures model data with several latent populations. Density estimation asks for an accurate distributional description even when individual components cannot be identified reliably.

Moitra and Valiant establish polynomial learnability for a fixed number of components, with dependence on k that does not meet the joint polynomial target. Existing atlas cards concern compression-style unsupervised learning, robustness for fixed k, or separated parameter estimation. Those are different statistical goals.

why: Resolve a central statistical-computational gap for latent-distribution learning without geometric separation.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
